public_rationale: The claim has two parts. The core point holds in part. Microsoft's CEO said in late 2025 that he had GPUs in inventory he could not plug in because data center shells were not ready. That fits construction lagging GPU purchases. The supporting point, that NVIDIA's GPU sales 'continue to accelerate dramatically every single quarter,' fails on NVIDIA's own FY2026 figures. In Q2 FY2026, total Data Center revenue grew only 5% and GPU compute revenue fell 1% from the prior quarter. Growth then sped up to 25% in Q3 but slowed to 22% in Q4. Sales grew strongly over the year, but they did not accelerate every quarter.
limitations: How large the construction lag is cannot be measured from public data, so 'dramatically' is untested.
The construction-lag support rests on one company's CEO.
Q2 FY2026 figures come from a news report of NVIDIA's release, not the release itself.

our_interpretation: The claim has two parts. (a) GPUs are being sold faster than data centers can be built to house them. (b) NVIDIA's GPU sales grew faster every quarter.

For (b), 'GPU sales' is read as NVIDIA's Data Center segment revenue and its compute (GPU) sub-line, the measure the speaker uses in his context. 'Accelerate every single quarter' is read as sales growing faster each quarter than the quarter before. Under a looser reading, sales at least rising every quarter, a quarter in which GPU compute sales fell would still contradict it.
For (a), credible statements from buyers or measurements showing purchased GPUs waiting on unbuilt or unpowered data center space count as support.
He names no period, so the target period is NVIDIA's fiscal 2026, the most recent full year of reports before the post, which he cites himself.
criteria.support_condition: NVIDIA's data center or GPU compute revenue rose faster each quarter of FY2026, and there is evidence that GPU purchases outran the data center space ready to house them.
criteria.contradiction_condition: NVIDIA's own figures show a FY2026 quarter in which GPU sales growth slowed or GPU compute revenue fell, and/or evidence shows data center construction keeping pace with GPU deliveries.
